title: Shifts and triangle closure of the pinned right-adjoint tensor locus
statement: Let $f:Z\to Y$, its derived categories, hRf, hO, hTensor, monoidal pullback structure, pullback adjunction a, and right adjunction adj to c satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-sc-right-adjoint-tensor-comparison-natural]. For quasi-coherent K, define P(K) to mean that there is a projection isomorphism pf with the pinned inverse equation of that node and that the adj-mate of pf followed by tensoring the counit and the right unitor is invertible. Then (1) for every integer n, P(A) and $B.obj\cong A.obj[n]$ imply P(B); (2) if an ambient distinguished triangle T has vertices isomorphic to A.obj, B.obj, C.obj respectively, then P(A) and P(B) imply P(C). No assumption on preservation of coproducts by c is needed, and neither coproduct nor retract closure is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0A9U, first two sentences of proof; Section 48.8, equation (48.8.0.1)

proof.text: Use the canonical natural comparison. K-flat pullback and tensor are exact with canonical shift comparisons. The right adjoint to the exact restricted derived pushforward is exact: transport shifts by the adjunction and test triangles with all representable Hom functors. The comparison respects shifts by the counit identities and monoidal coherence.

Conjugation by the shift comparisons and the specified ambient isomorphism transfers invertibility to B. For a distinguished ambient triangle with quasi-coherent vertices, lift it to the full subcategory. Apply the two exact functors and the comparison; use the morphism-of-triangles two-out-of-three lemma and the specified vertex isomorphisms. The pinned projection isomorphism is unique, so component invertibility gives the stated P memberships. Zero triangles and all integer shifts are included.
